title: Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control.
significance: While laboratory BCIs have decoded speech and cursor control with impressive accuracy, they have required constant technical supervision and lab environments, blocking real clinical translation. This work demonstrates that an intracortical BCI system can be operated independently by a patient at home for extended periods, supporting both naturalistic speech decoding and digital cursor control without expert oversight. This is a landmark proof of concept that addresses the critical gap between research prototypes and practical, patient-independent neurotechnology, showing that implantable BCIs can deliver genuine functional benefit and usability in real life, not just in controlled settings.

title: Responsive stimulation of the thalamus for idiopathic generalized epilepsy: Results of the randomized controlled NAUTILUS trial through 18 months.
significance: This trial demonstrates that responsive thalamic stimulation safely reduces seizures in drug-resistant generalized epilepsy patients who lack other effective treatment options.

title: Neuropixels Opto: combining high-resolution electrophysiology and optogenetics.
significance: This paper enables simultaneous high-resolution recording and spatially precise optogenetic manipulation of thousands of neurons, revolutionizing circuit neuroscience research capabilities.

title: Deep brain stimulation induces white matter remodeling and functional changes to brain-wide networks.
significance: This study reveals how DBS mechanically remodels white matter and reorganizes brain networks, providing crucial biological mechanisms explaining why this treatment alleviates depression.

title: Frequency-dependent cerebellar circuits independently gate social vocalizations and movement.
Simultaneous speech and gesture decoding for multimodal communication in paralysis.
significance: This work demonstrates simultaneous decoding of speech and gesture from a single high-density electrode array, enabling richer and more natural communication restoration for paralyzed individuals than speech-only BCIs. The multimodal approach better approximates how humans naturally communicate and represents a significant technical advance in neural decoding complexity and BCI fidelity. Clinical translation of this method could substantially improve quality of life for patients with severe paralysis from stroke or neurodegeneration.

title: Effective stimulation sites and networks for substantia nigra pars reticulata deep brain stimulation for auditory verbal hallucinations in schizophrenia.
significance: This work applies deep brain stimulation to a new psychiatric target (substantia nigra pars reticulata) for treatment-resistant schizophrenia, with acute outcome mapping using connectomics. It represents a clinically meaningful advance in understanding how DBS engages distributed brain networks to suppress symptoms, bridging device implantation with mechanistic circuit analysis. This directional progress in DBS applications and targeting refinement matters to practitioners developing psychiatric neuromodulation protocols.

title: Unifying Consent Standards for Implantable Brain-Computer Interfaces.
significance: Implantable BCIs differ fundamentally from established surgical procedures because they involve invasive recording of neural activity, continuous operation, and novel risks around autonomy, privacy, and identity. Current consent standards do not adequately address these unique challenges, creating ambiguity for clinicians and developers bringing iBCIs to patients. Establishing unified, neurotechnology-specific consent standards is essential for accelerating responsible clinical trials and regulatory approval of speech and motor BCIs.

title: Neurotechnological Natives and the Neurotechnology Shift: A Research Agenda for the Brain-as-Interface Era.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
significance: As brain-computer interfaces, neuromodulation devices, and neural sensors move beyond clinical settings into consumer and everyday applications, understanding the broader transformation in cognition, society, and technology adoption becomes critical for the field. This framing identifies the neurotechnology shift as a central challenge for practitioners, ethicists, and policymakers shaping how neurotechnology integrates into human life and work. It bridges device development with social and cultural feasibility.

title: Brain-computer interfaces and neuroprosthetics in the next era of neurosurgery.
significance: This review synthesizes the current state of brain-computer interfaces and neuroprosthetics as they move into real-world clinical deployment. It addresses the core neurotechnology challenge of translating invasive and minimally invasive neural interfaces from experimental settings into validated therapeutic systems. For neurotech practitioners, it provides essential context on the technical, surgical, and clinical requirements for BCI and neuroprosthetic systems across multiple restoration domains (communication, motor, sensory, autonomic).

title: Device-level comparisons of sensing and stimulation in implantable closed-loop neurostimulation for epilepsy.
Advancing data protections for implantable brain-computer interfaces.
significance: As implantable BCIs move from research prototypes into clinical practice, the rich neural signals they capture create unique privacy and security challenges beyond conventional health data. This review examines gaps in existing legal protections and proposes frameworks for safeguarding sensitive brain-derived information. Addressing data protection is essential infrastructure for clinical BCI deployment and directly impacts regulatory approval, commercialization, and patient trust in neurotechnology.
